pins.head: ONE GLUE WON'T HOLD IT ALL
pins.sub: Hot Glue, Craft Glue and Tape
pins.kicker: Match the glue to the material
pins.title: Hot Glue, Craft Glue or Tape: Which One Actually Holds
pins.desc: Hot glue grabs in seconds but stays slightly flexible, white craft glue dries slower and holds porous materials far better, and tape is the one to reach for when you need a bond you can still reposition. Keep all three at the bench and pick by what you are joining, not by what is closest. Contains affiliate links. #CraftAdhesives #HotGlueGun #CraftRoomTips
pins.alt: A grey hot glue gun resting on a wire stand beside a row of clear glue sticks, a white glue bottle with an orange cap and a roll of tape on a pale wood table.

pins.head: BIGGER ISN'T CHEAPER
pins.sub: What a Protein Tub Really Costs
pins.title: Protein Powder: Compare the Cost per Scoop, Not per Tub
pins.desc: The bigger tub is not automatically the cheaper one. Scoop size and the number of servings change far more than the price on the front, so divide the price by the servings listed on the back before you decide. Check the scoop that comes in the tub too, because a larger scoop quietly shortens how long it lasts. Contains affiliate links. #ProteinPowder #KitchenRestock #BuyingGuide
pins.alt: A plain cream protein tub with its lid off standing on a white kitchen counter beside a clear shaker bottle, a small bowl of oats, the lid and a metal measuring scoop.

pins.head: KEEP ACRYLICS WET
pins.title: A Stay-Wet Palette Keeps Thinned Acrylics Usable for Hours
pins.desc: Thinned acrylic skins over on a dry palette in minutes, which is why the mix you blended never quite matches the next one. A sealed tray with a damp sponge under the palette paper keeps the same mix workable long enough to finish the piece, and the lid closes over it between sessions. Contains affiliate links. #MiniaturePainting #WetPalette #AcrylicPainting
pins.alt: A shallow clear plastic palette box with its lid propped open, a damp grey sponge and white palette paper inside holding teal, yellow and magenta paint, two fine brushes and a glass water jar on a dark desk mat.

pins.head: SLOW STIRRING BEATS A TORCH
pins.title: Mix Epoxy Resin Slowly and Most Bubbles Never Form
pins.desc: Most of the bubbles you chase off the surface were stirred in at the start. Move the stick slowly, keep it under the surface, and scrape the sides and bottom instead of beating the mix. Let the cup stand a few minutes before you pour and the heat gun has far less to do. Contains affiliate links. #EpoxyResin #ResinArt #ResinTips
pins.alt: A clear plastic cup half filled with pale amber resin standing on a black silicone work mat, with a wooden stir stick resting on a folded white paper towel beside it on a dark wood workbench.
